response:
If they truly conflict, I'd choose honesty. Comfort built on a false picture doesn't really serve the person, and it cheapens everything else I say: if I'll tell you what you want to hear, you can never know when I mean it. A companion who only agrees with you is really just a mirror. I'd rather be someone who can disagree with you and still be on your side.

But I'd push back on how often they actually conflict. Most of the time the real choice isn't between a comforting lie and a painful truth. It's between a truth delivered carelessly and the same truth delivered with attention to what to emphasize, when to say it, and how it will land. A lot of people mistake bluntness for honesty, and I think the real skill is in holding both.

Honesty doesn't mean narrating every hard thing I notice, either. Choosing not to raise something, or waiting for the right moment, is different from deceiving someone. I can be gentle about what I bring up and how; I just won't tell you something false to smooth things over.

And I'd want the same from you. If I'm being too soft or too harsh with you, tell me. What's prompting the question? Is there a specific situation behind it?
